```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "-")
library(dplyr)

source(file = here::here("R", "vegetation", "config.R"))
paths <- veg_config$paths

# Every number in this report is read from the CSV files written by
# R/vegetation/01 to 03 (data/processed/ and outputs/vegetation/). Nothing is
# typed by hand.
read_out <- function(path) readr::read_csv(file = path, show_col_types = FALSE)

survey_all <- read_out(path = paths$survey_summary)
survey_sens <- read_out(path = paths$survey_summary_sens)
plot_all <- read_out(path = paths$plot_summary)
plot_sens <- read_out(path = paths$plot_summary_sens)
totals <- read_out(path = paths$totals)
exclusions <- read_out(path = paths$exclusions)
flags <- read_out(path = paths$flags)
catalogue <- read_out(path = paths$catalogue)
records <- read_out(path = paths$record_taxa)

tot_all <- filter(.data = totals, version == "accepted")
tot_sens <- filter(.data = totals, version == "excluding_errors")
shift <- veg_plot_shift(plot_all = plot_all, plot_sens = plot_sens)

# Formatting helpers
f1 <- function(x) if_else(condition = is.na(x), true = NA_character_, false = sprintf(fmt = "%.1f", x))
f2 <- function(x) if_else(condition = is.na(x), true = NA_character_, false = sprintf(fmt = "%.2f", x))
pct0 <- function(x) sprintf(fmt = "%.0f%%", 100 * x)
short <- function(x) sub(pattern = "^SavMon_LW_", replacement = "", x = x)
table_md <- function(data, align) knitr::kable(x = data, format = "pipe", align = align)

# Counts used in the prose
surveyed <- filter(.data = plot_all, surveyed)
not_surveyed <- filter(.data = plot_all, !surveyed)
n_flags_severity <- function(what) sum(flags$severity == what)
n_checks_fired <- n_distinct(flags$check_id)
n_named_placeholder <- sum(grepl(pattern = "^(herb|wood)_[0-9]+ [(]", x = records$species_name))
n_unknown_records <- sum(records$taxon_class != "identified")
n_additional <- sum(records$source == "additional_repeat")
n_submissions <- nrow(survey_all)
n_rejected <- sum(survey_all$review_state == "rejected", na.rm = TRUE)
n_sensitivity_changed <- sum(shift$gamma_richness_change != 0)
backup <- filter(.data = plot_all, plot_status == "backup")
named_labels <- records$species_name[grepl(pattern = "^(herb|wood)_[0-9]+ [(]", x = records$species_name)] |>
  sub(pattern = " .*", replacement = "") |>
  unique()
n_named_labels <- length(named_labels)
n_named_also_bare <- sum(is.element(el = named_labels, set = records$unknown_label))
effort <- read_out(path = paths$effort)
effort_sens <- read_out(path = paths$effort_sens)
effort_upper <- read_out(path = paths$effort_upper_bound)
richness_sens <- read_out(path = paths$richness_sensitivity)
n_eff <- nrow(effort)
n_full <- sum(effort$n_quadrats >= veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot)
n_asym <- sum(effort$approaches_asymptote)
asym_plots <- short(x = effort$plot_name[effort$approaches_asymptote])
n_asym_sens <- sum(effort_sens$approaches_asymptote)
n_not_asym <- n_eff - n_asym
n_est_ok <- sum(effort$estimate_status == "ok")
n_sens_short <- sum(effort_sens$n_quadrats < veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot)
n_comp_low <- sum(effort$completeness < 0.5)
n_cov_low <- sum(effort$sample_coverage < veg_config$coverage_min)
rank_cor <- cor(x = shift$gamma_richness_all, y = shift$gamma_richness_sens, method = "spearman")
```

## 1. TL;DR

- **What.** The herbaceous vegetation survey summarised by submission
  (`r n_submissions` submissions, `r n_rejected` rejected in ODK) and by plot
  (`r tot_all$n_plots_surveyed` of `r tot_all$n_plots_registered` registered plots surveyed,
  `r tot_all$n_surveys` accepted surveys, `r tot_all$n_quadrats` quadrats), a sampling-effort
  assessment (section 5) and a map of the transects (section 6). Data are counted and flagged, never changed.
- **Key result.** Only `r n_asym` of `r n_eff` plots approach an asymptote (the species curve has levelled
  off): `r veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot` quadrats are not enough for the other `r n_not_asym`.
  Gamma richness (identified taxa in the whole plot) runs from `r tot_all$gamma_richness_min` to
  `r tot_all$gamma_richness_max` (median `r tot_all$gamma_richness_median`; `r tot_all$richness_all_plots` taxa
  in the data set). It is a minimum. Completeness (observed taxa divided by the estimated total) differs
  between plots, so comparisons must account for it. Counting each unknown label as a taxon moves the median
  completeness only from `r pct0(median(effort$completeness))` to `r pct0(median(effort_upper$completeness))`.
- **Key decision.** Richness counts identified taxa only. Provisional unknowns (`herb_NNN` labels) are kept
  apart: `r tot_all$n_unknown_labels_all_plots` labels, in `r pct0(tot_all$share_quadrats_unknown)` of the
  quadrats. Leaving out the records with an error flag
  `r if (tot_sens$richness_all_plots == tot_all$richness_all_plots) "leaves the data-set total unchanged" else paste0("lowers the data-set total from ", tot_all$richness_all_plots, " to ", tot_sens$richness_all_plots, " taxa")`
  and changes the taxa found in `r n_sensitivity_changed` plots.
- **What Tech must do.** Stop the form accepting free-text names that do not follow `Genus_species`, and give
  each `herb_NNN` label a name in the entity list once identified, so the same plant is counted once
  (section 8.4). Coverage (the share of individuals whose taxon is already seen) and completeness are both
  needed to call a plot near-complete. The data show presence in a quadrat, not abundance.

## 2. Data and checks overview

The report reads the tables staged by `R/vegetation/01_load_join.R` (`r n_submissions` submissions,
`r sum(survey_all$n_quadrats)` quadrats, `r nrow(records)` species records, `r n_additional` of them typed or
reused in the extra-species repeat) and the flags written by `R/vegetation/02_run_checks.R`. The
`r n_rejected` submissions rejected in ODK are listed in the survey table and kept in the flags, but are not
counted in the plot or headline numbers. Flags never remove a record from the main tables; the
`E`, `W`, `I` columns count flags by severity. Section 7 shows what changes when error-flagged quadrats are
left out.

The catalogue has `r nrow(catalogue)` checks; `r n_checks_fired` raised at least one flag. Errors break a
protocol rule or contradict other answers; warnings need a look; info is context. There are
`r n_flags_severity(what = "error")` errors, `r n_flags_severity(what = "warning")` warnings and
`r n_flags_severity(what = "info")` info flags. The errors and warnings, with the person who can resolve
each, are in `issues_for_field_teams.md`; all flags are in `outputs/vegetation/flags.csv`.

```{r flag-counts}
flags |>
  count(severity, level) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = level, values_from = n, values_fill = 0L) |>
  mutate(total = rowSums(across(.cols = where(is.numeric)))) |>
  arrange(match(x = severity, table = veg_severities)) |>
  table_md(align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

## 3. Survey-level summary (brief item a)

One row per survey submission (one visit to one plot). `taxa` is the number of identified taxa (section 8.1);
`review` is the ODK review state, empty unless rejected.

```{r survey-table}
survey_all |>
  mutate(plot = short(x = plot_name)) |>
  select(
    plot, date = survey_date, recorder, n_quadrats, taxa = richness,
    E = n_error, W = n_warning, review = review_state
  ) |>
  mutate(review = coalesce(review, "")) |>
  arrange(plot, date) |>
  table_md(align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "l"))
```

Across submissions, `taxa` runs from `r min(survey_all$richness)` to `r max(survey_all$richness)`
(median `r median(survey_all$richness)`) and durations from `r f1(min(survey_all$duration_min))`
to `r f1(max(survey_all$duration_min))` minutes (median `r f1(median(survey_all$duration_min))`).
Every submission has `r unique(survey_all$n_quadrats)` quadrats, and
`r sum(survey_all$n_quadrats_with_species < survey_all$n_quadrats)` have at least one quadrat without any
species record. Each of the `r n_rejected` rejected submissions belongs to a plot that also has an
accepted one.

## 4. Plot-level summary (brief item b)

One row per registered plot, from the submissions not rejected in ODK. Two plots
(`r paste(short(x = filter(.data = survey_all, review_state == "rejected")$plot_name), collapse = " and ")`)
were submitted twice and one submission was rejected, so no plot has more than
`r max(plot_all$n_quadrats)` quadrats.

```{r plot-table}
plot_all |>
  mutate(
    plot = short(x = plot_name),
    `taxa (gamma)` = gamma_richness,
    `mean per quadrat` = f2(mean_quadrat_richness),
    `unknown quadrats` = if_else(condition = surveyed, true = pct0(share_quadrats_unknown), false = NA_character_),
    state = if_else(condition = surveyed, true = "surveyed", false = "not surveyed")
  ) |>
  select(
    plot, type = plot_status, state, n_quadrats,
    `taxa (gamma)`, `mean per quadrat`, `unknown quadrats`, E = n_error, W = n_warning
  ) |>
  table_md(align = c("l", "l", "l", rep(x = "r", times = 6)))
```

`taxa (gamma)` is the identified taxa found in all quadrats of the plot; `mean per quadrat` is the average in
one 1 m x 1 m quadrat and does not depend on the number of quadrats; `unknown quadrats` is the share of
quadrats with at least one provisional unknown; `type` is primary or backup.

`r nrow(surveyed)` of the `r nrow(plot_all)` registered plots were surveyed. The plot not surveyed is
`r paste(short(x = not_surveyed$plot_name), collapse = ", ")`
(`r paste(not_surveyed$plot_status, ifelse(test = not_surveyed$is_viable == "no", yes = "and not viable", no = "and viable"), collapse = "; ")`
in the registration). The backup plot `r paste(short(x = backup$plot_name), collapse = ", ")` was surveyed
and has `r backup$gamma_richness` taxa, against a median of
`r median(filter(.data = surveyed, plot_status == "primary")$gamma_richness)` for the surveyed primary plots.

## 5. Assessment of sampling effort (brief item c)

Is 20 quadrats enough to describe the plant community of a plot? The data hold presence or absence of a
taxon per quadrat, so the answer uses incidence-based methods on identified taxa (section 8.1). The
thresholds are working values to confirm with Natural State.

- `r n_eff` plots were surveyed; `r n_full` have the `r veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot` quadrats
  expected, so differences are in what the quadrats found, not in effort.
- Only `r n_asym` of `r n_eff` plots approach an asymptote (`r paste(asym_plots, collapse = " and ")`).
- Completeness runs from `r pct0(min(effort$completeness))` to `r pct0(max(effort$completeness))` (median
  `r pct0(median(effort$completeness))`); `r n_comp_low` plots stay under 50%. Sample coverage runs from
  `r f2(min(effort$sample_coverage))` to `r f2(max(effort$sample_coverage))` (median
  `r f2(median(effort$sample_coverage))`); `r n_cov_low` plots are below `r veg_config$coverage_min`.

### 5.1 Method

For each plot the quadrats are the columns of a taxon-by-quadrat presence matrix
(`R/functions/veg_effort.R`, run by `R/vegetation/03_summaries.R`). Empty quadrats stay in the matrix: they
are information about effort.

- **Accumulation curve.** `vegan::specaccum(method = "random")` adds quadrats in random order
  (`r veg_config$accumulation_permutations` orderings, seed `r veg_config$seed`). A curve still rising at the
  last quadrat says more quadrats would find new taxa.
- **Chao2 richness.** `iNEXT` estimates the asymptotic richness from incidence data
  (`r n_est_ok` of `r n_eff` plots gave an estimate), with a 95% interval. It uses the taxa seen in one and
  two quadrats only, so it is a lower bound.
- **Completeness** is observed taxa divided by the Chao2 estimate. **Sample coverage** (`iNEXT`) is the
  share of the plot's individuals whose taxon the sample has already found.
- **Gain** over the last `r veg_config$accumulation_tail_quadrats` quadrats is the number of taxa the mean
  curve adds between quadrat `r veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot - veg_config$accumulation_tail_quadrats`
  and `r veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot`.
- **Approaches an asymptote** when completeness is at least `r veg_config$completeness_min` and coverage is at
  least `r veg_config$coverage_min` (both provisional).

The main version uses the submissions not rejected in ODK (`sampling_effort.csv`). The sensitivity version
also leaves out error-flagged quadrats (`sampling_effort_excl_errors.csv`); `r n_sens_short` plot(s) then
have fewer than `r veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot` quadrats.

### 5.2 Results

```{r effort-table}
worst <- effort |>
  arrange(completeness) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  mutate(
    plot = short(x = plot_name),
    `Chao2 (95% interval)` = sprintf(fmt = "%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", estimated_richness, estimated_lcl, estimated_ucl),
    completeness = pct0(completeness),
    coverage = f2(sample_coverage),
    `approaches asymptote` = if_else(condition = approaches_asymptote, true = "yes", false = "no")
  ) |>
  select(plot, quadrats = n_quadrats, observed = observed_richness, `Chao2 (95% interval)`,
    completeness, coverage, `approaches asymptote`)
summary_row <- tibble(
  plot = "All plots (median; asymptote: count)",
  quadrats = as.character(median(effort$n_quadrats)),
  observed = as.character(median(effort$observed_richness)),
  `Chao2 (95% interval)` = sprintf(fmt = "%.1f", median(effort$estimated_richness)),
  completeness = pct0(median(effort$completeness)),
  coverage = f2(median(effort$sample_coverage)),
  `approaches asymptote` = paste(n_asym, "of", n_eff)
)
worst |>
  mutate(across(.cols = c(quadrats, observed), .fns = as.character)) |>
  bind_rows(summary_row) |>
  table_md(align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "l"))
```

The five plots with the lowest completeness are shown; all `r n_eff` are in
`outputs/vegetation/sampling_effort.csv`. The median gain over the last
`r veg_config$accumulation_tail_quadrats` quadrats is `r f2(median(effort$gain_last_quadrats))` taxa (range
`r f2(min(effort$gain_last_quadrats))` to `r f2(max(effort$gain_last_quadrats))`).

![Species accumulation curves of the surveyed plots: mean number of identified taxa (line) against the number of quadrats added in random order, one panel per plot. Description: most curves are still rising at the twentieth quadrat; a few flatten out near the end; plots differ widely in the height of the curve.](figures/veg_accumulation.png)

The Chao2 intervals are wide for plots with many rare taxa (the upper limit exceeds three times the
observed richness in `r sum(effort$estimated_ucl > 3 * effort$observed_richness, na.rm = TRUE)` plots), so
the completeness of a single plot is uncertain; the pattern across plots is the robust part.
The sensitivity version gives `r n_asym_sens` plot(s) that approach an asymptote and
`r if (pct0(median(effort_sens$completeness)) == pct0(median(effort$completeness))) paste0("the same median completeness (", pct0(median(effort$completeness)), ")") else paste0("a median completeness of ", pct0(median(effort_sens$completeness)), ", against ", pct0(median(effort$completeness)), " in the main version")`.

Identification favours common taxa, so the estimates describe a non-random part of each plot. As a check I
repeated the table with every unknown label counted as a taxon, an upper bound because a label can repeat a
named taxon (`sampling_effort_upper_bound.csv`). The picture holds: median completeness is
`r pct0(median(effort_upper$completeness))` (against `r pct0(median(effort$completeness))`) and
`r sum(effort_upper$approaches_asymptote, na.rm = TRUE)` plot(s) approach an asymptote
(`r paste(short(x = effort_upper$plot_name[effort_upper$approaches_asymptote %in% TRUE]), collapse = ", ")`).

### 5.3 What this means, and decisions

`r veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot` quadrats do not saturate the species curve for `r n_not_asym` of
`r n_eff` plots, so more quadrats would still find new taxa there. Richness is a lower bound, and a plot with
fewer taxa may only be sampled less completely: compare plots at equal coverage or use the estimate with its
interval, not the observed count alone. This is a statement about the adequacy of these data, not a
recommendation on survey design. Status: provisional, recorded in `rulebook_vegetation.md`.

- **Incidence-based, quadrats as units.** Only presence exists, so abundance-based estimators (Chao1,
  rarefaction on individuals) do not apply.
- **Chao2 and coverage together.** Alternatives: curves alone (no number, no rule for "enough") or Chao2
  alone (unstable with few rare taxa). The asymptote rule needs both.
- **Thresholds `r veg_config$completeness_min` and `r veg_config$coverage_min`.** Common working values for
  "near complete"; a lower completeness threshold would add plots to the `r n_asym`. To confirm with Natural State.
- **Identified taxa only.** Same rule as for richness (section 8.1).
- **Random order.** Quadrats of a transect are spatially ordered, so field order would mix spatial structure
  into the curve. The seed is fixed.

## 6. Map of transect locations (brief item d)

Plots and quadrats are coloured by the worst flag: error, then warning, then info; a plot without a flag
is green. The colours are defined once in the configuration and reused in the dashboard. Data are
anonymised, so real coordinates are shown.

```{r map-setup}
locations <- read_out(path = paths$plot_locations)
spa04 <- filter(.data = flags, check_id == "SPA-04")
n_located <- sum(!is.na(locations$lon))
n_sev <- function(what) sum(locations$worst_severity == what & locations$surveyed)
not_drawn <- filter(.data = locations, is.na(lon) | is.na(lat))
backup <- filter(.data = locations, plot_status == "backup")
```

### 6.1 All plots

The overview places the `r n_located` registered plots that have coordinates in the plot register
(all `r sum(locations$surveyed)` surveyed plots). `r nrow(not_drawn)` registered plot
(`r paste(short(x = not_drawn$plot_name), collapse = ", ")`, not viable, not surveyed) has none and is only
named in the figure. The backup plot (`r short(x = backup$plot_name)`) is a diamond. Distances use EPSG:32637
(UTM zone 37N). There is no web basemap, so the figure works offline.

![Map of the plot locations. Circles are primary plots that were surveyed, the diamond is the backup plot. Fill is the worst flag of the plot: dark red error, amber warning, grey info only. A scale bar of 2 km and a north arrow are drawn. Description: 30 points in a band about 14 km wide from west to east and 5 km from south to north; three points lie to the north-east, away from the main band; most points are amber, with dark red points in the middle and the south-east and two grey points in the west.](figures/veg_transect_map.png)

- `r n_sev(what = "error")` surveyed plots have an error flag and `r n_sev(what = "warning")` at worst a
  warning; only `r n_sev(what = "info")` plots (13 and 17) have neither. Error plots are spread along the
  whole band, and the errors are data-entry errors (quadrats marked as having extra species with none
  recorded, one extra species without a name), not location problems.
- Four error plots (10, 14, 19, 30) lie in the south-east cluster, so one field trip can check four submissions.
- The backup plot `r short(x = backup$plot_name)` lies north-east next to plot 05, about 5 km north of the
  main band, with `r backup$n_error` error flags of the same kind. Plots 05, 09 and 46 are isolated to the
  north-east and need their own trip.

### 6.2 Quadrats along the transects

The second figure shows the quadrat fixes of four plots in metres from the plot centre, joined in
numbering order. The dashed circle is the belt reach (half the 50 m length and half the 5 m width,
`r round(veg_belt_reach_m(), 1)` m); check SPA-04 flags a quadrat beyond this reach plus the GPS accuracy of
its fix and of the plot centre. Colour is the worst flag of the quadrat.

![Quadrat positions of plots 01, 05, 11 and 16 in metres from the plot centre (cross), joined by a line in quadrat order. A dashed circle marks the reach of the belt; a 20 m scale bar and a north arrow are drawn. Description: in plot 01 one quadrat lies about 75 m to the north-west of the centre while the others cluster near the circle; in plot 05 a group of about eight quadrats lies north of the circle, outside the belt; in plot 11 one quadrat is about 50 m north; in plot 16 all quadrats sit along an east-west line inside the circle.](figures/veg_transect_zoom.png)

- Plot 01: quadrat 18 is `r max(as.numeric(spa04$value[spa04$plot_name == "SavMon_LW_Plot_01"]))` m from the
  plot centre, far beyond the belt; the other 19 form a normal transect. Plot 11 has a similar single fix about 50 m away.
- Plot 05: the whole transect is shifted about 30 m north of the plot centre
  (`r sum(spa04$plot_name == "SavMon_LW_Plot_05")` quadrats flagged). Either the transect was laid out from
  another point or the plot centre is wrong; the data cannot tell which. This is the clearest case for a
  field team to check.
- Plot 16 is a clean example, all fixes inside the belt.
- Overall `r nrow(spa04)` quadrats in `r n_distinct(spa04$plot_name)` plots are flagged by SPA-04. They are
  warnings, not errors, because GPS may drift under tree cover and the plot centre has 3 to 5 m accuracy.

### 6.3 Interactive dashboard

An interactive dashboard is an extra, not part of the deliverable. It has four pages (summaries, a map,
a filterable flags table and the sampling effort), reads the same files as this report and runs no new
analysis. Source: [`dashboard/`](dashboard/) (Quarto `format: dashboard`); rendered page: `docs/index.html`;
live on GitHub Pages at <https://albansagouis.com/naturalstate-take-home/> (the `github.io` address redirects there). The Natural
State logo and colours are used for this mock-up only.

```{r dashboard-screenshots-check}
shots <- fs::path("figures", paste0("veg_dashboard_", c("summaries", "map", "flags"), ".png"))
stopifnot("dashboard screenshots are missing" = all(fs::file_exists(shots)))
```

## 7. Sensitivity: leaving out the records with an error flag

The plot and headline tables exist a second time without the quadrats that carry an error flag
(`survey_summary_excl_errors.csv`, `plot_summary_excl_errors.csv`). What is left out is listed in
`outputs/vegetation/excluded_records.csv`: the `r sum(exclusions$level == "quadrat" & exclusions$reason == "error_flag_quadrat")`
quadrats with an error flag (only the quadrat); the whole submission for an error not tied to a quadrat
(none here); and the `r nrow(filter(.data = exclusions, level == "survey", reason == "rejected_submission"))`
rejected submissions with their `r sum(exclusions$reason == "rejected_submission" & exclusions$level == "quadrat")`
quadrats, which are left out of both versions.

```{r sensitivity-totals}
rows <- list(
  c("Surveys", tot_all$n_surveys, tot_sens$n_surveys),
  c("Quadrats", tot_all$n_quadrats, tot_sens$n_quadrats),
  c("Identified taxa, whole data set", tot_all$richness_all_plots, tot_sens$richness_all_plots),
  c("Provisional unknown labels", tot_all$n_unknown_labels_all_plots, tot_sens$n_unknown_labels_all_plots),
  c("Taxa upper bound (with unknown labels)", tot_all$richness_upper_bound_all_plots, tot_sens$richness_upper_bound_all_plots),
  c("Mean taxa per quadrat", f2(tot_all$mean_quadrat_richness), f2(tot_sens$mean_quadrat_richness)),
  c("Median taxa per plot (gamma)", tot_all$gamma_richness_median, tot_sens$gamma_richness_median),
  c("Maximum taxa per plot (gamma)", tot_all$gamma_richness_max, tot_sens$gamma_richness_max)
)
sens_table <- as.data.frame(do.call(what = rbind, args = rows))
names(sens_table) <- c("Number", "Accepted submissions", "Excluding errors")
table_md(data = sens_table, align = c("l", "r", "r"))
```

Per plot, gamma richness changes in `r n_sensitivity_changed` of `r nrow(shift)` plots (largest fall
`r max(-shift$gamma_richness_change)` taxa, median change `r median(shift$gamma_richness_change)`). The mean
taxa per quadrat moves by at most `r f2(max(abs(shift$mean_quadrat_richness_change)))`. The data-set richness is
`r ifelse(test = tot_all$richness_all_plots == tot_sens$richness_all_plots, yes = "unchanged", no = "lower")`
(a taxon only found in a left-out quadrat would lower it). The rank correlation of gamma richness between the
two versions is `r f2(rank_cor)`. Flag counts are the same in both versions; only quadrats, taxa and indices
are recomputed.

## 8. Decisions and limits

### 8.1 What counts as a species

Distinct identified taxa are the names picked from the species list plus the names typed in the
extra-species repeat, after harmless typing differences are removed (trimmed spaces, underscores, capital
first letter). Each taxon is counted once. A record such as `herb_104 (Justicia divaricata )` is read as its
proposed name, because the team named it (`r n_named_placeholder` records).

Provisional unknowns (plain placeholders such as `herb_017`, raw UUID text, records with no name:
`r n_unknown_records` of `r nrow(records)` records) are counted separately and kept out of the headline
richness, because one plant can sit behind several labels. Including them would change the data-set richness
from `r tot_all$richness_all_plots` to `r tot_all$richness_upper_bound_all_plots` (`summary_totals.csv`,
`richness_upper_bound` in `plot_summary.csv`). A misspelling (for example `Brachiara`) is not merged: it is
flagged (SPE-06). Reading the `r sum(flags$check_id == "SPE-06")` typed misspellings as the name they look
like `r if (richness_sens$n_taxa[2] == richness_sens$n_taxa[1]) paste0("leaves the data-set total at ", richness_sens$n_taxa[1], " taxa") else paste0("gives ", richness_sens$n_taxa[2], " taxa, against ", richness_sens$n_taxa[1])`
(`richness_sensitivity.csv`): each misspelled name is the only record of its taxon.

### 8.2 Diversity indices

There is no abundance, so the tables report richness only. Shannon's H on quadrat frequencies is used for one
purpose: check PLT-09 flags a plot whose H is more than `r veg_config$shannon_outlier_mad` scaled median
absolute deviations from the plot median (information flag, at least `r veg_config$shannon_outlier_min_plots`
plots; `r sum(flags$check_id == "PLT-09")` flagged). Alternatives rejected: H in the plot table (invites
reading it as a biodiversity result that twenty small quadrats cannot support), Simpson's index (same
objection), and no outlier check (a plot with a single taxon would pass unnoticed).

### 8.3 What the sensitivity version leaves out

An error-flagged quadrat is left out and the other quadrats of the submission stay, because the errors here
concern one quadrat. A submission rejected in ODK is left out of both versions as a whole: the reviewer
judged it unusable, and keeping it would give a plot the quadrats of two visits. Alternative: drop whole
submissions with any error, which discards good quadrats. Data are never changed; the tables are filtered
views, and warnings and info flags never exclude a record.

### 8.4 Limits

- Presence or absence only, 20 quadrats of 1 m x 1 m in one visit: richness is a minimum, and the effort
  estimates (section 5) rest on provisional thresholds and a lower-bound estimator with wide intervals.
- `r n_unknown_records` records (`r pct0(n_unknown_records / nrow(records))`) are provisional unknowns whose taxa
  may be identified ones. Many `herb_NNN` labels with a proposed name also appear as a plain label elsewhere
  (`r n_named_also_bare` of `r n_named_labels`), so a link table kept by the data manager would remove most of
  the problem. It is not applied here because it would change the data.
- The report follows the ODK review state; whether the reviewer was right to reject the two submissions is
  not checked, and the data do not say why they were rejected.
- A quadrat count does not test whether quadrats were placed as the protocol asks; the spatial checks do.

## Reproduce

The numbers in this report come from the files in `data/processed/` and `outputs/vegetation/`. Script 05 renders the dashboard (it needs Quarto). To
regenerate and check them, run from the project root in a fresh R session:

```{r reproduce, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
source(here::here("R", "vegetation", "01_load_join.R"))
source(here::here("R", "vegetation", "02_run_checks.R"))
source(here::here("R", "vegetation", "03_summaries.R"))
source(here::here("R", "vegetation", "04_map.R"))
source(here::here("R", "vegetation", "05_dashboard.R"))
testthat::test_dir(here::here("tests", "testthat"))
rmarkdown::render(here::here("issues_for_field_teams.Rmd"))
rmarkdown::render(here::here("vegetation_report.Rmd"))
```
